1→# Karma AOV and Render Pass Setup
     2→
     3→## What are AOVs?
     4→AOV = Arbitrary Output Variable. Extra render passes beyond beauty (RGBA).
     5→Used for compositing: separate diffuse, specular, emission, etc.
     6→
     7→## Setting Up AOVs in Karma
     8→
     9→### Using Karma Render Properties LOP
    10→1. Create `karmarenderproperties` LOP in /stage
    11→2. In "Image Output" section, add extra image planes
    12→3. Each plane = one AOV
    13→
    14→### Common AOV Names (Karma)
    15→| AOV Name | Description |
    16→|----------|-------------|
    17→| `C` or `beauty` | Final combined beauty pass |
    18→| `direct_diffuse` | Direct diffuse illumination |
    19→| `indirect_diffuse` | Indirect (bounced) diffuse |
    20→| `direct_specular` | Direct specular/reflection |
    21→| `indirect_specular` | Indirect specular |
    22→| `direct_emission` | Emissive surfaces |
    23→| `sss` | Subsurface scattering |
    24→| `direct_coat` | Clearcoat direct |
    25→| `albedo` | Surface albedo (base color) |
    26→| `N` | World-space normals |
    27→| `P` | World-space position |
    28→| `Z` or `depth` | Camera depth |
    29→| `motionvector` | 2D motion vectors |

     9→| `ifd` | Mantra renderer | `vm_picture`, `camera` |
    10→| `opengl` | OpenGL flipbook | `picture`, `camera` |

    12→## Karma Engines
    13→
    14→| Engine | Parm Value | Speed | Quality | Use Case |
    15→|--------|-----------|-------|---------|----------|
    16→| Karma XPU | `xpu` | Fast (GPU) | Production | Default for all work |
    17→| Karma CPU | `cpu` | Slow | Reference | Volumes, SSS, complex shading |

    20→- Nested dielectrics (glass inside liquid)
    21→- Complex SSS (skin with multiple scatter profiles)

1→# Karma AOV and Render Pass Setup
     2→
     3→## What are AOVs?
     4→AOV = Arbitrary Output Variable. Extra render passes beyond beauty (RGBA).
     5→Used for compositing: separate diffuse, specular, emission, etc.
     6→
     7→## Setting Up AOVs in Karma
     8→
     9→### Using Karma Render Properties LOP
    10→1. Create `karmarenderproperties` LOP in /stage
    11→2. In "Image Output" section, add extra image planes
    12→3. Each plane = one AOV
    13→
    14→### Common AOV Names (Karma)
    15→| AOV Name | Description |
    16→|----------|-------------|
    17→| `C` or `beauty` | Final combined beauty pass |
    18→| `direct_diffuse` | Direct diffuse illumination |
    19→| `indirect_diffuse` | Indirect (bounced) diffuse |
    20→| `direct_specular` | Direct specular/reflection |
    21→| `indirect_specular` | Indirect specular |
    22→| `direct_emission` | Emissive surfaces |
    23→| `sss` | Subsurface scattering |
    24→| `direct_coat` | Clearcoat direct |
    25→| `albedo` | Surface albedo (base color) |
    26→| `N` | World-space normals |
    27→| `P` | World-space position |
    28→| `Z` or `depth` | Camera depth |
    29→| `motionvector` | 2D motion vectors |
    30→| `crypto_material` | Cryptomatte by material |
    31→| `crypto_object` | Cryptomatte by object |
    32→| `crypto_asset` | Cryptomatte by asset |
    33→
    34→## Cryptomatte Setup
    35→Cryptomatte generates ID mattes for compositing selection.
    36→1. Add `crypto_material` and/or `crypto_object` AOV
    37→2. In Nuke/Comp: use Cryptomatte node to select objects by clicking
    38→3. No manual matte creation needed
    39→
    40→## Denoising AOVs
    41→Karma XPU supports built-in denoising:
    42→- `denoise_albedo` - Albedo for denoiser guide
    43→- `denoise_normal` - Normal for denoiser guide
    44→- Enable via `karmarenderproperties` "Denoising" section
    45→
    46→## Deep Output
    47→Deep compositing preserves per-sample depth:
    48→1. Set output format to `.exr` with deep flag
    49→2. Enable "Deep Output" in render properties
    50→3. Allows depth-correct compositing in Nuke
    51→
    52→## Light Groups
    53→Separate AOVs per light or light group:
    54→1. Tag lights with `lightGroup` attribute
    55→2. AOVs auto-generated as `{aov}_{lightgroup}`
    56→3. Enables per-light adjustment in comp
    57→
    58→## Render Resolution
    59→- usdrender ROP: `res_user1` (width), `res_user2` (height)
    60→- karma ROP: `resolutionx`, `resolutiony`
    61→- Override: `override_res` = `"specific"` to enable custom resolution
    62→
    63→## Compositing Workflow (AOV Rebuild)
    64→
    65→In Nuke/comp, rebuild beauty from AOVs:
    66→```
    67→beauty = direct_diffuse + indirect_diffuse + direct_specular + indirect_specular + direct_emission + sss
    68→```
    69→This lets you adjust each lighting contribution independently in post.
    70→
    71→## Tips
    72→- Always render `crypto_object` + `crypto_material` for comp flexibility
    73→- Use `N` and `P` passes for relighting and depth effects in comp
    74→- `motionvector` pass enables 2D motion blur in comp (cheaper than 3D)
    75→- For animation: render at least 128 samples with variance oracle for clean AOVs
    76→

1→# Karma Rendering Reference
     2→
     3→## ROP Types for /out
     4→
     5→| Type Name | Description | Key Parms |
     6→|-----------|-------------|-----------|
     7→| `karma` | Native Karma driver | `picture`, `camera`, `engine` |
     8→| `usdrender` | USD-based render driver | `loppath`, `outputimage`, `override_camera` |
     9→| `ifd` | Mantra renderer | `vm_picture`, `camera` |
    10→| `opengl` | OpenGL flipbook | `picture`, `camera` |
    11→
    12→## Karma Engines
    13→
    14→| Engine | Parm Value | Speed | Quality | Use Case |
    15→|--------|-----------|-------|---------|----------|
    16→| Karma XPU | `xpu` | Fast (GPU) | Production | Default for all work |
    17→| Karma CPU | `cpu` | Slow | Reference | Volumes, SSS, complex shading |
    18→
    19→**When to use CPU over XPU:**
    20→- Nested dielectrics (glass inside liquid)
    21→- Complex SSS (skin with multiple scatter profiles)
    22→- Volume rendering with many scattering events
    23→- When XPU produces fireflies that won't converge
    24→
    25→## Karma ROP in /out -- Setup Checklist
    26→
    27→1. Create: `hou.node("/out").createNode("usdrender", "render")`
    28→2. Set `loppath` to LOP display node (e.g., `/stage/karma_settings`)
    29→3. Set `renderer` to `BRAY_HdKarma`
    30→4. Set `override_camera` to USD prim path (e.g., `/cameras/render_cam`)
    31→5. Set `override_res` to `"specific"` (string, not int!)
    32→6. Set `res_user1` (width) and `res_user2` (height)
    33→7. Set `outputimage` to output file path
    34→
    35→## IMPORTANT: output_file kwarg
    36→
    37→`rop.render(output_file=...)` does NOT work for usdrender ROPs.
    38→Must set `outputimage` or `picture` parm directly on the node.
    39→
    40→## Karma Render Properties LOP
    41→
    42→Create `karmarenderproperties` in /stage for quality control.
    43→
    44→### Sample Settings
    45→
    46→| Parameter | Name | Default | Production | Preview |
    47→|-----------|------|---------|-----------|---------|
    48→| Max Ray Samples | `karma:global:pathtracedsamples` | 64 | 128-256 | 16-32 |
    49→| Min Ray Samples | `karma:global:minpathtracedsamples` | 1 | 16 | 1 |
    50→| Pixel Oracle | `karma:global:pixeloracle` | `uniform` | `variance` | `uniform` |
    51→| Convergence Threshold | `karma:global:convergencethreshold` | 0.01 | 0.005 | 0.05 |
    52→| Max Diffuse Bounces | `karma:global:diffuselimit` | 2 | 4-6 | 1 |
    53→| Max Specular Bounces | `karma:global:reflectlimit` | 4 | 6-8 | 2 |
    54→| Volume Step Rate | `karma:global:volumesteprate` | 0.25 | 0.5-1.0 | 0.1 |
    55→
    56→### Denoising
    57→
    58→Karma XPU has built-in OIDN denoiser:
    59→- Enable: `karma:global:enabledenoise` = 1
    60→- Requires: `denoise_albedo` and `denoise_normal` AOVs
    61→- For animation: use temporal denoising to avoid flickering
    62→
    63→### Motion Blur
    64→
    65→| Parameter | Name | Default |
    66→|-----------|------|---------|
    67→| Enable | `karma:object:xform_motionsamples` | 2 (on) |
    68→| Shutter Open | `karma:global:shutteropen` | -0.25 |
    69→| Shutter Close | `karma:global:shutterclose` | 0.25 |
    70→| Deformation Blur | `karma:object:geo_motionsamples` | 1 (off, set to 2 for on) |
    71→
    72→## Camera Path
    73→
    74→Camera must be specified as USD prim path: `/cameras/render_cam`
    75→NOT as Houdini node path: `/stage/render_cam`
    76→
    77→## Resolution Override
    78→
    79→The `override_res` parameter is a STRING MENU:
    80→- `""` -- None (use USD settings)
    81→- `"scale"` -- Percentage of resolution
    82→- `"specific"` -- Specific resolution (enables res_user1/res_user2)
    83→
    84→## Karma XPU File Flush
    85→
    86→Karma XPU has a 10-15 second delay between render() returning and the
    87→file being fully written to disk. Poll with 0.25s interval for up to 15s.
    88→
    89→## Common Render Issues
    90→
    91→### Black render
    92→1. Check camera is assigned (`override_camera` is a USD prim path)
    93→2. Check `loppath` points to a valid LOP node with a stage
    94→3. Check lights exist and have exposure > 0
    95→4. Check objects aren't set to `invisible`
    96→
    97→### Fireflies (bright pixels)
    98→1. Increase max samples to 256+
    99→2. Enable pixel oracle `variance` mode
   100→3. Lower convergence threshold to 0.001
   101→4. Check for intensity > 1.0 on lights (Lighting Law violation)
   102→5. Check roughness isn't exactly 0.0 (use 0.001 minimum)
   103→
   104→### Slow renders
   105→1. Reduce max ray bounces (diffuse=2, specular=4 for preview)
   106→2. Use `variance` pixel oracle (skips converged pixels)
   107→3. Lower resolution for iteration
   108→4. Disable motion blur and DOF for layout
   109→5. Use XPU instead of CPU
   110→
   111→### Noisy volumes
   112→1. Increase `volumesteprate` to 0.5-1.0
   113→2. Increase max samples
   114→3. Check volume density isn't too low (invisible but still scattering)
   115→
   116→## Output Formats
   117→
   118→| Format | Extension | Use Case |
   119→|--------|-----------|----------|
   120→| EXR (half) | `.exr` | Production (16-bit float, AOVs) |
   121→| EXR (deep) | `.exr` | Deep compositing |
   122→| JPEG | `.jpg` | Quick preview only |
   123→| PNG | `.png` | Web preview (8-bit, lossless) |
   124→| TIFF | `.tif` | Print / high-bit-depth |
   125→
   126→## Render via Synapse
   127→
   128→```python
   129→# Quick preview render
   130→render(width=1280, height=720)
   131→
   132→# Production render with specific ROP
   133→render(node="/out/karma_final", width=1920, height=1080)
   134→
   135→# Check render settings
   136→render_settings(node="/stage/karmarenderproperties1")
   137→
   138→# Override samples for preview
   139→render_settings(node="/stage/karmarenderproperties1", settings={
   140→    "karma:global:pathtracedsamples": 32,
   141→    "karma:global:pixeloracle": "variance"
   142→})
   143→```

    40→### Types of Render Noise
    41→| Noise Type | Appearance | Fix |

    43→| General noise | Grain across image | Increase max samples (128 -> 256) |
    44→| Shadow noise | Noisy in dark areas | Increase min samples, use variance oracle |
    45→| Specular noise | Fireflies on reflective surfaces | Enable clamping, increase specular bounces |
    46→| Volume noise | Grain in smoke/fog | Increase volume step rate (0.5 -> 1.0) |

    79→
    80→### Common Lighting Issues
    81→| Issue | Visual Sign | Fix |
    82→|-------|------------|-----|
    83→| Flat lighting | No shadows, uniform brightness | Increase key:fill ratio (3:1 or higher) |
    84→| Harsh lighting | Deep black shadows | Add fill light, raise fill exposure |
    85→| No depth separation | Subject blends with background | Add rim light, adjust exposure |
    86→| Hot spots | Blown white areas | Lower light exposure, check intensity=1.0 |
    87→| Wrong mood | Too bright for dramatic scene | Increase key:fill ratio, lower env exposure |
    88→| Color cast | Unwanted color tint | Check light colors, environment HDRI white balance |
    89→
    90→### Lighting by Scenario
    91→| Scenario | Key:Fill Ratio | Env Exposure | Mood |
    92→|----------|---------------|--------------|------|
    93→| Product beauty | 2:1 | 1.0 | Clean, inviting |
    94→| Broadcast | 3:1 | 1.0 | Professional, clear |
    95→| Dramatic | 4:1 | 0.0 | Moody, cinematic |
    96→| Horror/noir | 8:1+ | -1.0 | Dark, tense |
    97→| Overcast | 1.5:1 | 2.0 | Soft, natural |
    98→
    99→## Material Quality
   100→
   101→### What to Check
   102→- **Roughness range**: Pure 0.0 roughness causes fireflies. Use 0.001 minimum.
   103→- **Metalness**: Should be 0.0 (dielectric) or 1.0 (metal). Avoid 0.3-0.7 range (physically incorrect).
   104→- **Base color value**: Metals have colored specular, not colored diffuse. Dark diffuse + high metalness = correct metal.
   105→- **Fresnel**: At grazing angles, all materials become more reflective. If edges look wrong, check IOR.
   106→
   107→### Common Material Issues
   108→| Issue | Visual Sign | Fix |
   109→|-------|------------|-----|
   110→| Plastic look | Too uniform specular | Add roughness variation via texture |
   111→| Fireflies | Bright pixel artifacts | Set roughness minimum 0.001, lower max specular bounces |
   112→| Black metal | Metal with no reflection | Add environment light (dome light) for reflections |
   113→| Glowing edges | Incorrect fresnel/IOR | Check material IOR setting, verify normal direction |
   114→| Flat surface | No micro-detail | Add roughness map, displacement, or bump map |
   115→
   116→## Composition Analysis
   117→
   118→### Rule of Thirds
   119→- Key subjects should align with 1/3 grid lines
   120→- Camera focal point at intersection of thirds
   121→- Negative space on opposite side of subject
   122→
   123→### Depth Cues
   124→- **Atmospheric perspective**: Distant objects slightly hazier (volume fog)
   125→- **DOF**: Shallow depth of field draws focus (lower fStop value)
   126→- **Scale reference**: Include recognizable objects for scale
   127→- **Occlusion**: Foreground elements overlapping background adds depth
   128→
   129→## Iteration Workflow
   130→
   131→### Fast Iteration (Layout/Blocking)
   132→1. Render at 640x360 with 16 samples, uniform oracle
   133→2. Check composition, lighting direction, overall exposure
   134→3. Adjust light positions and exposures
   135→4. Re-render until composition reads well
   136→
   137→### Quality Iteration (Lookdev)
   138→1. Render at 1280x720 with 64 samples, variance oracle
   139→2. Check material quality, noise, color
   140→3. Adjust materials, add detail textures
   141→4. Enable denoiser for quick clean preview
   142→
   143→### Final Quality
   144→1. Render at full resolution with 256+ samples
   145→2. Enable all AOVs for compositing
   146→3. Verify no clipping, noise, or artifacts
   147→4. Export EXR with AOVs for post-production
   148→
   149→## Render-Analyze-Adjust Loop
   150→
   151→The most productive workflow with Synapse:
   152→1. **Render**: Use `houdini_render` at preview quality
   153→2. **Analyze**: Look at the returned image — check exposure, noise, composition
   154→3. **Adjust**: Modify light exposure, camera position, material properties
   155→4. **Re-render**: Verify the adjustment improved the image
   156→5. **Iterate**: Repeat until satisfied, then render at final quality

    55→### Transform Order

   113→| Arc | Strength | LOP Node | Use Case |
